sentences.text: Butyribacter intestini was described from strain TF01-11, a non-motile, Gram-stain-positive, obligate anaerobic bacterium isolated from human faeces.
The end products of glucose fermentation by that strain were butyric acid and a small amount of acetic acid, and it is a member of the family Lachnospiraceae.
In a cohort of 6419 participants followed for incident pneumonia, the relative abundance of Butyribacter intestini was inversely associated with pneumonia risk.
A metagenomic study reported that a group of patients with post-stroke cognitive impairment and type 2 diabetes showed depletion of butyrate-producing taxa including Butyribacter intestini.
